in_arabic.name: محمد
in_arabic.meaning: محمد تعریف کرتا ہے، প্রশংসا کا پાત્ર ہے
in_arabic.long_meaning: محمد نام اللہ کے نبی کا نام ہے، جو تمام مخلوقات کے لئے ایک مثالی نمونہ ہے۔ یہ نام محمد بن عبداللہ کے لئے استعمال ہوا، جو اسلام کے بنیادی پیغمبر ہیں۔ اس نام کی اصولی معنی প্রশংসا کے مستحق ہونے کی وجہ سے ہے، کیونکہ وہ اپنے اخلاق، طرز عمل، اور عظیم صفات کی وجہ سے প্রশংسا کا پات્ર ہیں۔

in_urdu.name: محمد
in_urdu.meaning: محمد معنی تعریف کا پات્ર، قابل ستائش
in_urdu.long_meaning: محمد ایک ایسا نام ہے جو اسلامی تاریخ میں انتہائی اہمیت کا حامل ہے، کیونکہ یہ نام رسول اللہ کی شناخت ہے۔ نام محمد، عربی زبان کے الفاظ 'حمید' سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہوتا ہے 'ستائش کے قابل' یا 'تعریف کا پاتر'۔ اسلامی روایات کے مطابق، یہ نام ان کی غیرمعمولی صفات، بہترین کردار، اور مثالی طرز عمل کی وجہ سے دیا گیا تھا۔

in_hindi.name: मोहम्मद
in_hindi.meaning: मोहम्मद मतलब प्रशंसा के योग्य, स्तुतियोग्य
in_hindi.long_meaning: मोहम्मद नाम इस्लामी परंपरा में बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है, क्योंकि यह नाम पैगंबर मोहम्मद का है। यह नाम अरबी भाषा के शब्दों से निकला है, जिसका अर्थ है 'प्रशंसा के योग्य' या 'स्तुतियोग्य'। इस्लामी परंपराओं के अनुसार, यह नाम उनकी अद्वितीय विशेषताओं, उत्कृष्ट चरित्र, और अनुकरणीय आचरण के कारण दिया गया था।

in_pashto.name: محمد
in_pashto.meaning: محمد د معنی د ستاینې وړ، د تعریف سړی
in_pashto.long_meaning: محمد نوم د اسلامي تاريخ لپاره ډېر مهم دی، ځکه دا نوم د رسول الله نوم دی. دا نوم د عربي کلمو څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې معنی یې 'د ستاینې وړ' یا 'د تعریف سړی' دی. د اسلامي رواياتو له مخې، دا نوم د هغه د ځانګړو ځانګړتیاوو، غوره چلند، او د نمونې په توګه د ورکړل شوي دی.

in_english.name: Mihammad
in_english.long_meaning: The name Mihammad is derived from the Arabic root 'h-m-d', which means 'to praise'. It is a name given to the Prophet of Islam, Muhammad, who is considered a paragon of virtues and a model for humanity. The name signifies 'praiseworthy', 'glorified', or 'worthy of praise', reflecting the esteemed qualities and character of the Prophet.

data.cultural_impact: Muhammad is the Islamic prophet and the founder of the Islamic religion, considered by Muslims to be the last messenger of God in the line of prophets beginning with Adam and continuing through Abraham, Moses, Jesus and others. His name holds great reverence and respect, and is synonymous with Islam itself. Muhammad's teachings, practices, and interpretations of the Islamic revelation—contained in the Quran—form the basis for the Islamic faith.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Muhammad carries a deep spiritual significance for Muslims. Muslims believe that Allah (God) named their prophet Muhammad as a sign of favor and blessing, and the name serves as a reminder of the infinite kindness and mercy of Allah. The name represents the ultimate goal of every Muslim's journey—to be a servant of Allah, to seek His pleasure, and to strive for His approval—as Muhammad did throughout his life. Muslims strive to emulate Muhammad's exemplary character, known as the Sunnah, and to follow his teachings and practices to attain nearness to Allah. The name Muhammad serves as a constant reminder of the divine presence and compassion in every Muslim's life and action.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: According to Islamic tradition, Muhammad was born in Mecca around 570 AD, and is believed to be the last prophet of God in the line of prophets including Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.
historical_references.context: Muhammad is considered the founder of Islam, receiving divine revelations from Allah through the angel Gabriel, which were compiled in the Holy Quran. He was also a social and political leader, and his teachings became a major influence on Arab and Islamic civilizations.

historical_references.reference: Before his prophethood, Muhammad was a merchant and a leader in his community. He was known for his honesty and integrity, and was revered as a protector of the Kaaba, the holiest site in Islam. In 610 AD, Muhammad received his first revelation from the angel Gabriel, and began to preach the teachings of Islam.
historical_references.context: Muhammad's early followers were mainly from the lower classes of Meccan society, and they faced persecution from the ruling elite. In 622 AD, Muhammad and his followers migrated to Medina, where they established a peaceful community and gained many converts. This event is known as the Hijra, and marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar.
